framing: Stop paying for the same prompt twice
paragraphs: Production prompts repeat themselves. The same instructions, tool schemas, and reference text lead request after request, and without a cache the GPU recomputes all of it every time.

Prefix caching keeps the results and reuses them. The idea fits in a sentence, and the details decide whether it pays. One changed token near the top invalidates everything after it, a cache helps only the worker that holds it, and a shared entry must never serve a tenant it wasn't written for.
We'll build the keys block by block, work out when a paid cache write breaks even, and look at a case where a hit makes the user wait longer.
You'll come away able to order a prompt so it caches, read hit-rate numbers without fooling yourself, and decide when to send a request to a warm worker and when to let it go cold.
outcomes: Compute the input work a prefix saves across cold and warm requests.
Design prompts and cache keys that reuse work without crossing into another tenant's cache.
Tell a good cache hit from a bad routing decision, using token-level metrics.
question: A cache hit removes more than a second of work, yet the user waits longer for the first token. How can both be true?
